catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class sets an over-voltage protection threshold of a power supply. cap.device.configure.v1 is a state-write class, but the upstream class defines only the set_ovp() setter and no OVP getter or status field (rigol.py:105-114), so a state write could not show an observable effect (TCAP-003) without inventing a readback; the package uses an x-cap id with an inline input and output schema and reports the channel and the value sent.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/jasapp__rigol --backend fake: all nine gates pass with no findings and no warnings, and the evidence state is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. No hardware was attached and native.py was never imported or run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper PythonObjectDriver (family python-object) with decision direct-driver; the package is a decorated direct Driver over rigol:RigolDP832A (the decision is unchanged). A PythonObjectDriver read map takes no arguments, while the upstream getters take a channel number (get_output, get_voltage_setpoint, get_current_setpoint, measure_voltage, measure_current and measure_power all take channel, rigol.py:62-103), so a family command table cannot express the three-channel state; no wire syntax was changed. COVERED: for channels 1, 2 and 3 the output state, voltage set point, current set point, measured voltage, measured current and measured power are read state; the three output states are writable through cap.device.configure.v1; the six voltage/current set points are writable through cap.device.configure.v1 with operator_required limits; set_ovp and set_ocp are x-cap actions that call the upstream setters; the e-stop is all_off(), the upstream native stop that turns channels 1, 2 and 3 off (rigol.py:129-132). NOT COVERED: the OVP and OCP thresholds have no upstream getter or status field, so they are not read back (the action output reports the value sent); the upstream status() ChannelStatus is not exposed as one state field because it is an object; the raw command()/query() transport and the configure() convenience method are not exposed to agents; no hardware run, no recording, and no wire-level conformance were done. LIMITS AND PROVENANCE: the clone has no README, no docs directory and no text manual, and it states no voltage, current or protection range, so all six set-point bounds and both protection-threshold bounds are Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json is a deliberately narrow example overlay (0 to 5 V, 0 to 1 A) and is not a device rating, and without an operator overlay every one of those writes and actions is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. The only sourced limit is the channel number of the two protection actions, 1 to 3, cited to the upstream all_off() loop (rigol.py:131). Every Fact cites a line of the clone at commit 602b8623f820f6b4db4d225b1d66f11b3bbb6d6a; the gate reports no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning, and no PDF was cited or read. SAFETY: the driver is R1, equal to the card floor and the cap.device.configure.v1 class floor; no independent hardware e-stop is stated in the clone and none is claimed, so @estop is the software native stop all_off() and the declared safe state is all three channel outputs off. At R1 the loader does not refuse the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written package, so a human must review it and set reviewed_by before anyone passes --allow-hardware. LICENSE: the upstream licence is NOASSERTION with license_class unknown (the clone has no LICENSE file) and publish_review is required; no upstream code is vendored or imported by the fake. MOCK PATH: the card preferred a fake; fake.py is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording, and every starting value and reply in it is marked # placeholder and is not a Fact, a Limit or a reference. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the authored package; gate.digest is the digest the check printed.
